title: Ban on non-compete, no-poach and wage-fixing clauses
summary: An exposure draft bill, consulted on from 7 September to 2 October 2026, would ban non-compete clauses for workers below an income threshold and ban no-poach and wage-fixing agreements, intended from 2027. Not legislated.

instruments.title: Exposure draft: Treasury Laws Amendment (Banning Unfair Non-Competes) Bill 2026 (title as reported)

direction_rationale: Removing restraints lets workers move to rivals or start their own firms, raising job mobility, wages and spin-off entry.
comparison: Workers below versus above the income threshold (threshold not confirmed)
notes: Not yet law. A candidate for a plan registered before commencement.

verified.notes: No commencement date. Consultation dates from Treasury's consultation page.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Would ban non-compete clauses for workers earning below a threshold, and no-poach and wage-fixing agreements, from 2027. About one in five workers has a non-compete; removing them lets workers move to rivals or start firms. Not yet legislated.

marks.reason: Removes a barrier to moving between jobs for a large share of the workforce.
Workers can leave to start competing firms.

assessment.confidence_note: The Productivity Commission modelled a 0.10 to 0.19% rise in GDP from non-compete reform.
